capabilities.capability: The zero-config pool runs one handler thread until a job has waited: only one idle thread per lane spins, a push wakes nobody while a thread of the lane is busy or spinning, a ring that holds a job and whose pop count has not moved for `POOL_WAKE_AGE_NS` has a parked sibling woken by the loop (a ring being drained is left alone, however deep — on a GIL build; without a GIL the pool is parallel, `set_parallel`: a push wakes a parked thread whenever there is one and the wait counts from the push), and every thread is woken by name on a channel of its own, most recently parked first (`M0_POOL_ELASTIC=0` restores the eager wakes)
capabilities.evidence: `test_offload.mojo:test_a_job_behind_a_slow_sibling_is_taken_once_the_loop_wakes_a_parked_one` (every PR) — the rules beside it in the same file: `test_submit_wakes_nobody_while_a_sibling_is_busy`, `test_submit_wakes_nobody_while_a_sibling_spins`, `test_a_burst_into_a_parked_lane_wakes_one_thread`, `test_a_ring_being_drained_is_never_stalled`, `test_on_a_free_threaded_interpreter_the_pool_wakes_eagerly_and_counts_from_the_push`, `test_sequential_jobs_with_idle_gaps_stay_on_one_thread`, `test_a_wake_lands_on_the_parked_threads_own_channel`, and the knob-off arm `test_elastic_off_restores_the_chained_wake`; the isolation the rules must keep is C5's smoke. The measurement, both platforms: docs/notes/elastic-pool.md

capabilities.capability: Workers sharing one listener share its connections: the worker that wins an accept passes the connection to the least-loaded sibling over a pre-fork `SCM_RIGHTS` channel, so a burst of keep-alive connections spreads across `--workers N` to within 2:1 on both platforms, forked or spawned, at no cost to a single worker (`M0_ACCEPT_SHARE=0` restores the bare race)
capabilities.evidence: `Smoke test accept sharing` (every PR) — two rounds of a 32-connection burst per worker mode must land within 2:1, the doctor must report `accept_sharing` for two workers and not for one, and on macOS the knob-off arm must skew; the descriptor passing and the load policy: `test_accept_share.mojo:test_a_connection_passes_between_two_workers_with_its_peer`. The measurement, both platforms before and after: docs/notes/accept-sharing.md

capabilities.capability: A job pushed to a pool lane whose threads are parked or inside slow views is taken without a lost wake, on Linux, where the kernel wakes one waiter and the only lost pool wake ever caught reproduced
capabilities.evidence: `stress-pool` (pre-release) — in the `m0lin` container, once per shipped wake mode (the GIL rules, `M0_POOL_PARALLEL=1`, `M0_POOL_ELASTIC=0`): `scripts/probes/phase5_probe.py` runs `smoke-django-realtime` phase 5 twenty times with a fresh server each round — two 1.5 s views in flight, a hold taken on a pool thread, its subscriber must be registered half a second later; 2 of 10 rounds failed on the ring's first build (docs/notes/pool-ring-handoff.md) — and `scripts/probes/hold_race_probe.py` opens forty holds while three clients keep the loop busy. The deterministic half is E17's unit tests; the isolation is C5's smoke

capabilities.capability: A view that RELEASES the GIL runs in parallel across `--blocking-threads`, and one that holds it does not — the pool's N threads do N things at once only when the work inside the view drops the interpreter lock
capabilities.evidence: `Smoke test pool parallelism` (every PR) — `bareapp`'s `/work` is one hashlib call over two buffer sizes either side of `HASHLIB_GIL_MINSIZE`, so the lock is the only variable: two at once cost 1.02x one for the releasing mode and 2.01x for the holding one, and a server given a single handler thread sends both to 2.0x. C5 is the isolation half of the same pool; this is the concurrency half, which C5 passes without. What it decides in practice: Core ML's `predict` holds the lock and an embedding app gained nothing from more handler threads, MAX releases it and the same app scaled — docs/notes/gil-and-the-handler-pool.md
